title: 第5章 武道与魔法第6章 假装筑基
slug: 我在西幻世界独断万古
content_zh:
第二天一早，季天是被敲门声吵醒的。
他睁开眼睛的时候，天刚蒙蒙亮，窗外训练场上空无一人，沙地上还残留着昨夜露水的痕迹。
他昨晚睡得不算踏实——床太软了，被子太暖了，和村子里的稻草垫子完全不是一回事。
可让他睡不踏实的真正的原因是，他满脑子都是那个火球。
橘红色的、安静燃烧的、违反了一切物理常识，但却像修仙之人基础操作的火球。
它不需要燃料，不需要氧气，就那么凭空悬浮在短杖的顶端，像是一颗被驯服的星星。
他坐起来，正准备穿鞋，门就被推开了。
艾琳娜站在门口，怀里抱着一本厚得能砸死人的书。
她今天换了一身浅紫色的裙子，领口的花纹比昨天那件更复杂，两个辫子编得一丝不苟，发尾的蝴蝶结换成了淡紫色的。
她整个人看起来像是从画里走出来的——如果画里的人会用那种居高临下看小动物的眼神看你。
她走进来，把那本书往季天床上一扔。
“砰”的一声，床板都震了一下。
季天低头看了看那本书。皮面精装，烫金字体，书页的边缘刷着一层金粉，在晨光下闪闪发亮。
封面上写着几个他还不认识的字，但根据厚度来判断，这本书少说也有五百页。
他抬头看向艾琳娜，意思是，“是说要陪你出去玩吗？这又是唱哪出？”
艾琳娜双手叉腰，下巴微微扬起。这个姿势让她看起来比实际年龄更小一些，但那双灰蓝色的眼睛里闪着一种狡黠的光。
“哼，”她鼻腔里发出一声很酷的轻哼，“昨晚看我使用魔法，你眼神都直了。”
季天没说话。
“你以为我没注意到？”艾琳娜的嘴角翘起来，带着一丝得意，“那种眼神我见多了——又羡慕又渴望，像是饿了三天的小狗看到肉骨头。”
“……我没有。”

“你有——”艾琳娜看向季天的眼睛，斩钉截铁地说，“你眼睛都快贴到我法杖上了。”
季天沉默了一秒。
他确实对那个火球很感兴趣，但他觉得自己当时的表情应该没那么夸张。
不过看艾琳娜那副笃定的样子，他懒得反驳。
“你也想学魔法吧？”艾琳娜说，语气从得意变成了一种故作随意的漫不经心，“反正也是闲着，不如培养个魔法师玩玩。”
她说话的时候不看季天，只是偏过头去看窗外，装做在欣赏训练场上那片空荡荡的沙地，眼角余光却分明在往这边瞟。
季天瞬间就明白了。
她想教他魔法。
不是“顺便”或“闲着没事”。
她专门挑了一大早、专门抱了这本厚书、专门跑到他房间里来——就为了教他魔法。
但她不想让他觉得她是专门来教他的。
所以她要摆出一副“反正我闲着也是闲着”“培养个魔法师玩玩”的态度，好像这只是一时兴起，好像他学不学都无所谓。
季天觉得有点好笑。
但他没有笑出来，他看得出，这位大小姐的脸皮其实很薄。
艾琳娜从书架上抽出另一本薄得多的小册子，和那本大部头一起摞在床边。
“《魔法基础理论》，第一章到第三章。”她重新恢复了那种发号施令的语气，双手叉腰，居高临下地看着坐在床边的季天，“三天之内看完，然后我来考你。要是看不懂——”
她顿了顿，似乎在思考一个足够有威慑力的惩罚。
“要是看不懂，你就去厨房削土豆。削一个月。”
季天低头看了看那本《魔法基础理论》。
他翻开第一页。

然后愣住了。
content_en:
Early the next morning, Ji Tian was woken up by a knock on the door.
When he opened his eyes, it was just dawn, the training ground outside the window was empty, and traces of last night's dew still remained on the sand.
He didn't sleep well last night - the bed was too soft and the quilt was too warm, which was completely different from the straw mattresses in the village.
But the real reason why he couldn't sleep well was that his mind was filled with that fireball.
Orange-red, burning quietly, it violates all common sense of physics, but it is like a fireball that is basically operated by a cultivator.
It doesn't need fuel or oxygen. It just floats on the top of the short staff out of thin air, like a tamed star.
He sat up and was about to put on his shoes when the door was pushed open.
Elena stood at the door, holding a book in her arms that was so thick that it could crush someone to death.
She changed into a light purple dress today. The pattern on the neckline was more complicated than the one yesterday. Her two braids were meticulously braided, and the bow at the end of her hair was replaced with a lavender one.
She looked like she had stepped out of a painting—if the person in the painting looked at you condescendingly at a small animal.
She walked in and threw the book on Ji Tian's bed.
There was a "bang" sound, and the bed board shook.
Ji Tian lowered his head and looked at the book. It is leather-bound and has gilded fonts. The edges of the pages are brushed with a layer of gold powder, which shines in the morning light.
There were a few words written on the cover that he didn't recognize yet, but judging from the thickness, the book had at least five hundred pages.
He raised his head and looked at Elena, meaning, "Are you saying that I want to go out with you? Where do you mean this?"
Elena put her hands on her hips and raised her chin slightly. This posture made her look younger than her actual age, but there was a cunning light in her gray-blue eyes.
"Hmph," she let out a cool hum in her nasal cavity, "you saw me using magic last night, and your eyes were straightened."
Ji Tian said nothing.
"You think I didn't notice?" Elena's lips curled up with a hint of pride, "I've seen that look too many times - envious and eager, like a puppy that has been hungry for three days seeing meat and bones."
"...I didn't."
"You have-" Elena looked into Ji Tian's eyes and said decisively, "Your eyes are almost on my staff."
Ji Tian was silent for a second.
He was indeed interested in the fireball, but he felt that his expression at that time should not be that exaggerated.
But looking at Elena's determined look, he didn't bother to refute.
"You also want to learn magic, right?" Elena said, her tone changing from being proud to a casual insouciance, "I have nothing to do anyway, so why not train a magician for fun."
She didn't look at Ji Tian when she spoke, but just turned her head to look out the window, pretending to be admiring the empty sand on the training ground, but she was clearly glancing this way from the corner of her eye.
Ji Tian understood instantly.
She wants to teach him magic.
Not "by the way" or "just having nothing to do."
She specially picked this early morning, specially picked up this thick book, and specially ran to his room - just to teach him magic.
But she didn't want him to think that she was here specifically to teach him.
So she had to adopt the attitude of "I'm free anyway" and "training a magician for fun", as if it was just a whim, as if it didn't matter whether he learned or not.
Ji Tian found it a bit funny.
But he didn't laugh. He could see that this young lady was actually very thin-skinned.
Elena pulled out another much thinner booklet from the bookshelf and stacked it with the tome beside the bed.
"Basic Theory of Magic, Chapters 1 to 3." She regained her commanding tone, put her hands on her hips, and looked condescendingly at Ji Tian who was sitting beside the bed, "Read it within three days, and then I'll take a test on you. If you can't understand—"
She paused, as if thinking of a punishment that would be sufficiently deterrent.
"If you don't understand, go to the kitchenPeel potatoes. Cut for a month. "
Ji Tian lowered his head and looked at the "Basic Theory of Magic".
He turned to the first page.
Then he froze.
